question: Which anatomical feature makes young women more vulnerable to sexually transmitted infections?
explanation: Cervical ectopy exposes delicate columnar cells on the outer cervix, making it easier for germs to invade the tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why are females biologically more prone to sexually transmitted infections than males?

options.A: Faster cellular turnover rates in the vagina
options.B: Larger mucosal surface area in the reproductive tract
options.C: Lower temperature in the pelvic cavity
options.D: Higher local production of protective antibodies

explanation: The large and moist mucosal lining of the female reproductive tract provides a welcoming environment for germs to settle and enter the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is it called when germs spread upward from the vagina into the fallopian tubes?
explanation: An ascending infection happens when microorganisms travel up from the lower reproductive tract into the upper pelvic organs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h2)

question: A pregnant patient passes an untreated cervical infection to her newborn during delivery. What type of transmission is this?
explanation: Vertical transmission is the passing of an infection from a mother to her baby during pregnancy or childbirth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which sexually transmitted infection is caused by a flagellated protozoan parasite?
explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by Trichomonas vaginalis, a single-celled protozoan parasite that uses flagella to move. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h3)

question: What classic finding is often seen on the cervix during a speculum examination of a patient with trichomoniasis?
explanation: Trichomoniasis often causes tiny red spots on the cervix, which clinicians commonly call a strawberry cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which viral infection is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?
explanation: High-risk strains of the Human Papillomavirus are the primary cause of cell changes that can lead to cervical cancer. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: What type of skin lesion is most typical of an active primary Herpes Simplex Virus outbreak?

options.A: Painless indurated ulcers with raised firm borders
options.B: Painful fluid-filled vesicles that rupture into shallow ulcers
options.C: Dry scaly plaques with central clearing

explanation: Herpes simplex infections usually show up as painful, clustered blisters that break open to form tender sores. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the most sensitive and commonly used lab test to detect Chlamydia and Gonorrhoea?
explanation: Nucleic acid amplification tests detect the genetic material of germs with very high accuracy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why is taking a detailed sexual history an important part of the nursing assessment?

options.A: It provides definitive proof of partner infidelity
options.B: It replaces the need for physical pelvic examinations
options.C: It determines the exact date of infection contraction
options.D: It guides targeted diagnostic testing and identifies transmission risks

explanation: A careful sexual history helps the nurse figure out which specific screening tests are needed based on possible exposure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h5)

question: A patient treated for chlamydia asks if she can have sex right away after taking her single-dose antibiotic. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Resume relations as soon as the burning sensation stops
options.B: Wait seven days and ensure your partner has also been treated
options.C: Wait until your next menstrual cycle begins
options.D: Resume immediately since the medication works right away

explanation: Patients must avoid sexual contact for seven days after treatment and make sure partners are treated to stop passing the infection back and forth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why is treating sexual partners essential when managing sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: To verify the accuracy of the initial laboratory diagnosis
options.B: To prevent reinfection and break the community cycle of transmission
options.C: To satisfy legal reporting requirements for all minor infections
options.D: To punish individuals who engage in risky sexual behaviours

explanation: Treating sexual partners at the same time stops people from passing the infection back and forth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h6)

question: What major reproductive problem is often linked to untreated chlamydia or gonorrhoea?
explanation: Untreated lower tract infections can travel up into the upper reproductive organs and cause pelvic inflammatory disease. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: How do untreated sores from sexually transmitted infections increase the risk of getting HIV?

options.A: By stimulating the liver to produce antibodies that destroy immune cells
options.B: By increasing the total volume of vaginal secretions produced daily
options.C: By altering the normal hormonal balance of the menstrual cycle
options.D: By breaking the mucosal barrier and providing direct entry into the bloodstream

explanation: Open sores and inflammation create direct openings for viruses like HIV to enter the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: When should the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine be given for the best protection?

options.A: After the first episode of genital warts
options.B: Immediately after a positive screening test
options.C: During the third trimester of pregnancy

explanation: The HPV vaccine works best when given before any possible exposure to the virus through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h8)

question: Which nursing action is an example of secondary prevention for sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Screening asymptomatic women during routine clinic visits
options.B: Teaching safe sex practices to community youth groups
options.C: Administering the human papillomavirus vaccine to school children
options.D: Providing emergency housing for high-risk populations

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and prompt treatment of hidden or symptom-free diseases to stop them from getting worse. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h8)
